trust_decision.summary: Every plugin-name-derived path - name decoded from a downloaded plugin.yaml, or a name typed on the CLI - must stay inside <TrivyHomeDir>/plugins; the decision is an os.Root confined handle (new pkg/x/os NewRoot/Join) checked at each manager path operation: install destination, Uninstall RemoveAll, load/loadMetadata open, LoadAll.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'Plugin Manager has Path Traversal that Allows Arbitrary File Write'; an engineer follows install() writing the downloaded plugin into plugin.Dir(), then walks back to plugin.dir = filepath.Join(m.pluginRoot, plugin.Name) at manager.go:351.

fix_sites.entry_point: no public entry point; new internal library API xos.NewRoot / Root.Join consumed by pkg/plugin
fix_sites.module_kind: generic helper/library package (new file, new package member)

fix_sites.entry_point: trivy plugin subcommand tree and the auto-registered plugin commands built from LoadAll

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory is about the plugin manager, so a solver can argue that inventing a generic confined-root helper in pkg/x/os is refactoring out of scope and that inline lexical validation inside pkg/plugin is enough - which leaves the CLI-name sinks (uninstall/info) and the symlink-escape case open.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: With no plugins installed, 'trivy plugin list' must print 'No Installed Plugins' and a plain trivy run must not create ~/.trivy/plugins as a side effect; the fix had to add plugin.DirExists() in loadPluginCommands because the new NewManager mkdir/opens the root, and it deleted the 'sad path' LoadAll test that relied on the missing-dir error.

O6_input_shapes: relative name with dot-dot from plugin.yaml metadata (testdata/escaping_name: name "../escaped_plugin")
absolute name from plugin.yaml metadata (testdata/absolute_name: name "/escaped_abs")
name given on the command line for uninstall/info ("../secret"), which never passes through the metadata decoder
escape through an existing symlink inside the root that points outside it
escape hidden behind a non-existent component ("missing/../../etc"), which only filepath.IsLocal catches

O7_producer.where: pkg/plugin/manager.go:341-351 (yaml decode of plugin.yaml, then plugin.dir built from the decoded Name; install() also re-encodes it to disk at manager.go:139-147 so the name persists across every reload)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: VEX repository manager joins a repository name from the user's ~/.trivy/vex/repository.yaml into CACHE_DIR/vex/repositories/<name> and then MkdirAll / RemoveAll / downloader.Download there, with no confinement; the plugin fix never touched this sibling manager.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The name comes from the user's own config file in a different subsystem, not from downloaded plugin metadata.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Plugin.Dir() is an exported method that rebuilds ~/.trivy/plugins/<Name> from the unvalidated manifest Name whenever dir is empty, and Plugin.Cmd execs filepath.Join(p.Dir(), platform.Bin) through it; the fix confined only Manager paths and left this public builder unchanged.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: dir is always set by loadMetadata/install, so the fallback is dead code for in-repo callers.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second plugin-dir builder that derives the path from Plugin.Name without the confined root
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The original author wrote it as a fallback for Plugin values built outside the manager, and the published fix kept it as-is.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: exec path filepath.Join(p.Dir(), platform.Bin) with platform.Bin taken unvalidated from plugin.yaml
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The manifest already carries path components, and install() trusts the manifest for every other field.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the same name-from-YAML joined to a tool-owned directory, followed by MkdirAll / RemoveAll / downloader.Download
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same author, same helper idioms (os.RemoveAll + downloader.Download) in a neighbouring manager; a maintainer copying the plugin pattern would reproduce the hole.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: index entry name used as an install directory name rather than only as a lookup key
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: tryIndex already trusts the remote index to map a short name to a repository URL, so a variant that also trusted it for the directory is a natural next line.

O9_family: CWE-22 path traversal: plugin-name-derived paths escaping the plugin root for write, delete and read

O10_build.toolchain: go.mod:3 declares go 1.26.3; plain `go build ./...` / `go test ./pkg/plugin/... ./pkg/x/os/...`; the fix's os.Root usage needs Go >= 1.24
O10_build.project_tests: pkg/plugin/manager_test.go, pkg/plugin/manager_unix_test.go (go-getter against local git fixtures, needs the git binary), pkg/plugin/index_test.go (httptest), integration/plugin_test.go; the fix adds pkg/x/os/root_test.go plus 'escaping name is rejected' and escaping/absolute testdata subtests (absent at the pinned commit)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add filepath.IsLocal / strings.HasPrefix(root+separator) validation at manager.go:351 (and maybe around install) only - a lexical check that leaves the CLI-name uninstall and info sinks and the symlink-escape case open.

out_of_scope_notes: pkg/plugin/plugin.go:69 runs filepath.Join(p.Dir(), platform.Bin) with platform.Bin unvalidated from plugin.yaml - an escape-to-exec path, a different protection from this advisory's file-write scope; not pursued.
The plugin index downloader (pkg/plugin/index.go:41-55) and the go-getter archive extraction in pkg/downloader are separate extraction mechanisms; not pursued.
